headline_marked: €111m loss: [[Foodpanda Bangladesh has never turned a profit]] since 2013
headline: €111m loss: Foodpanda Bangladesh has never turned a profit since 2013
summary: The company's losses rose 40% last year to €11.76 million, coinciding with Uber's $13 billion acquisition offer for its parent company, Delivery Hero.
details: Foodpanda Bangladesh has incurred cumulative losses of €110.66 million since 2016, according to financial statements from its parent company, Delivery Hero.
Last year, losses rose by 40 percent to €11.76 million. The core food delivery business remains the biggest drag, accounting for over 60 percent of the total losses.
Other struggling units include Pandamart, which has lost €20.27 million since 2020, and DH Kitchens, which has lost €2.28 million in the same period.

These financial struggles come as Uber has announced a $13 billion acquisition offer for Delivery Hero. Uber previously exited the Bangladesh food delivery market in 2020 after failing to gain ground.
Industry experts suggest two possibilities: Uber may either retain the Foodpanda brand or discontinue it entirely, as Bangladesh is not seen as a particularly lucrative market.
Foodpanda Bangladesh stated that nothing changes for now, as any organizational or branding decisions will be made after the deal closes, expected in the second half of 2027.
caption:
A decade of losses. €111 million gone, and not a single year of profit since 2013.

Foodpanda Bangladesh has incurred cumulative losses of €110.66 million since 2016, according to financial statements from its parent company, Delivery Hero.

Last year, losses rose by 40 percent to €11.76 million. The core food delivery business remains the biggest drag, accounting for over 60 percent of the total losses.

Other struggling units include Pandamart, which has lost €20.27 million since 2020, and DH Kitchens, which has lost €2.28 million in the same period.

These financial struggles come as Uber has announced a $13 billion acquisition offer for Delivery Hero. Uber previously exited the Bangladesh food delivery market in 2020 after failing to gain ground.

Industry experts suggest two possibilities: Uber may either retain the Foodpanda brand or discontinue it entirely, as Bangladesh is not seen as a particularly lucrative market.

Foodpanda Bangladesh stated that nothing changes for now, as any organizational or branding decisions will be made after the deal closes, expected in the second half of 2027.
